requirement:
The instructions supplied under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered
page before submitting its answer. They explain how to select the tags of
excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.
Finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.
rationale:
The subject requires the first-search `instructions` text to cover four things. Each one is asserted in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]`. The test is marked `{test}` for this requirement.

- **Call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting.** The test takes `instructions` from the first `search_text` result, which has an empty `matches` list. It asserts the text contains "Before submitting, close every delivered search page" and "finish_search".
- **How to select the tags of excerpts used as evidence.** It asserts the text contains "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read".
- **How to pass `used: []` when none contributed.** It asserts the text contains "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result".
- **Finishing records the inputs without fetching more source.** It asserts the text contains "without reading more source".

The same instructions string is also asserted on the first `search_structure` result of a separate session (`assert_eq!(page["instructions"], instructions)`) and on a fresh session's `hits`. Later searches and continuation pages are asserted to omit the field. Those omissions belong to the parent `instructions` requirement, but they confirm the content is delivered as intended.

The assertions are substring checks on the key phrases, not full-text equality. That is enough for the content obligations here, because each required element has its own phrase asserted. The test also exercises the described behaviour: `finish_search` with `used: []` and with a selected tag, and the resulting dependencies. I found no uncovered obligation in the subject's text.
